title: Kestrel and the Orchard
premise: Kestrel Vale, a ghostwriter who has spent her life hiding behind other people's words, takes a seasonal job cataloguing the failing Winterbourne orchard-vineyard, where owner Cyrus Winterbourne guards his inherited debts behind a wall of cold efficiency. When a town tradition pairs anonymous pen-pals for the harvest season, the two enemies are matched without knowing it, and through letters they each fall for the person they can't stand in person. As bankruptcy proceedings threaten to sell the orchard out from under them, their identities are exposed at the worst possible moment, shattering both trusts. In the end, Kestrel must choose between disappearing into anonymity again or staying past the last train to help Cyrus save the orchard—and together they turn the debt-ridden estate into a co-op run by the found family of workers who never gave up on it.
about_author: Coral Ashgrove is the pen name of a former orchard hand who wrote love letters for illiterate farmworkers in exchange for pie. She lives somewhere with unreliable cell service and strong opinions about cider.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Fleeing a career scandal, she arrives in Alder Hollow to catalogue the Winterbourne estate, planning to stay invisible until spring. Her first meeting with Cyrus is a collision of pride: he mistakes her for an auditor, she lets him. Emotional beat: guarded self-containment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He surveys rotting vines and foreclosure notices, convinced emotion is a muscle he's trained into submission. He assigns Kestrel the impossible task of inventorying an orchard worth nothing. Emotional beat: grief disguised as contempt for his late father's failures.

chapters.title: Anonymous Correspondents Wanted
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The town's Harvest Letters tradition pairs residents anonymously; Kestrel signs up under a whim, craving a voice that isn't a client's. Her first letter receives a reply so sharp it stings—yet she writes back. Emotional beat: the thrill of being seen without being known.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Working beside Kestrel in the rows, Cyrus finds her competence infuriating and her silences disarming. He vents his frustrations about 'a meddling letter-writer' to her face, not knowing she is that writer. Emotional beat: grudging respect taking root like a sucker shoot.

chapters.title: What the Letters Confess
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The correspondence deepens; her pen-pal admits fear of becoming his father, and Kestrel recognizes Cyrus in every line. Meanwhile the orchard crew—a found family of misfits—adopts her, and she almost tells Cyrus the truth. Emotional beat: identity cracking open under warmth.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. An early frost threatens the crop; Kestrel works all night beside him lighting smudge pots, and something nearly happens between them before he retreats. The bank moves up the auction date. Emotional beat: desire and dread entwining as time runs short.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the Harvest Letters reading, Cyrus is called to read his final letter aloud—and realizes mid-verse that his correspondent is standing in the crowd. His public humiliation curdles into accusation: she played him. Emotional beat: betrayal, exposure, the death of trust.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus throws himself into losing the orchard gracefully, refusing Kestrel's apology and her plan to rally the workers. But rereading her letters, he sees the woman in them was never false. Emotional beat: pride crumbling into honest reckoning.

chapters.title: Auction Day
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the courthouse auction, Kestrel gambles everything—her savings, her name, her ghostwriting confession published in the town paper—to bid alongside the workers' pooled wages. Cyrus arrives at the last moment, not to stop her but to stand beside her. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered publicly, and answered.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Shared closing movement. The orchard becomes a worker-owned co-op; Kestrel chooses to stay, writing her first story under her own name. On the platform where she once planned her escape, Cyrus asks her to miss no more trains. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not what we're given, but who stays.
